newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB, hurt by bad loan fears, biggest loser on TSE.
newsitem.headline: NCB, hurt by bad loan fears, biggest loser on TSE.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd came under heavy selling pressure and became the biggest percentage loser on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Monday morning on persisting worries about bad loan problems at banks, traders said.
As of 0053 GMT, the bank's shares were down 40 yen at 224 yen in turnover of 2.18 million.

Overshadowing Japanese banking shares is a widespread belief that lower overall stocks market prices will be a further setback for financial institutions already facing the difficult task of tackling mountains of bad loans.

According to a recent estimate by Goldman Sachs (Japan), if the key Nikkei average falls below 16,751, appraisal losses in Nippon Credit's stock holdings should offset its expected operating profits in the current fiscal year to March 31, 1997.
